title: Retention verification dashboards + alerts (TTL lag, purge success/failures)
creator: Allison Grant
related_links: GitHub (redwood): PR-28489 background purge job framework
GitHub (redwood): PR-28540 add retention verification metrics
GitHub (observability-pack): PR-441 add retention compliance dashboards
Slack: #eng-sre thread 1740662244 retention purge jobs observability requirements
description:
Goal
Ship a standard, low-cardinality set of dashboards and alerts to verify retention enforcement across core stores (request/response logs + audit logs first). This is required for:
- GA readiness for retention controls (prove TTL enforcement is happening)
- Support/SRE triage (detect backlog + failures after incidents/maintenance)
- Compliance reporting pack evidence (exportable screenshots + time-windowed stats)

Scope (v1)
1) Dashboards
- "Retention Controls — Overview" (exec/SRE view)
  - TTL lag heatmap by store x region
  - Purge throughput (rows deleted / sec) by store
  - Purge failures (rate + top error reasons)
  - Backlog proxy (ttl_lag_seconds p95/p99 + oldest eligible record age where available)
- "Retention Controls — Purge Jobs" (operator view)
  - Job runs over time (success/failure) by job_name + store
  - Duration p50/p95
  - Retry counts and throttling events (from structured logs)
  - Safety limits hit (batch size / max rows per run)
- "Retention Controls — Policy Drift" (sanity view)
  - % of tenants with evaluator errors / fallback-to-default
  - Policy cache invalidation counts and evaluator latency
  - Mismatch detector: config TTL vs effective TTL applied in job labels (where emitted)

2) Alerts (initial set)
- TTL lag SLO breach (page)
  - Condition: ttl_lag_seconds p99 > 24h for 30m (per store+region) in prod
  - Rationale: indicates purge job stalled/backlogged materially beyond intended SLA
- Purge failures elevated (page)
  - Condition: purge_failures rate > 1% for 15m AND purge_job_runs_total > min volume
  - Include top error_code dimension in annotation (from log-based metric)
- Purge job not running (ticket)
  - Condition: no successful purge run in 2h for a given store+region in prod
- Cardinality guardrail (ticket)
  - Condition: metric series count > threshold for retention metric namespace (prevents accidental tenant_id label rollout)

Dependencies / prerequisites
- Metrics emitted by purge job framework + store implementations (ENG-18433/ENG-18434). Expected canonical metrics (names per PR-28540):
  - ttl_lag_seconds{store,region,env}
  - purge_rows_deleted_total{store,region,env}
  - purge_failures_total{store,region,env,error_code}
  - purge_job_run_duration_seconds{job_name,store,region,env,outcome}
  - purge_job_runs_total{job_name,store,region,env,outcome}
- Log-based signals:
  - Structured logs from purge framework including error_code, retryable, throttled, limit_hit

Cardinality requirements (hard constraints)
- No tenant_id/customer_id labels in default dashboards/alerts.
- Allowed labels: env, region, store, job_name, outcome, error_code (error_code must be normalized to a small fixed set).
- For tenant-specific debugging, rely on tracing/log search and on-demand ad hoc queries (not time-series labels).

Acceptance criteria
- Dashboards available in prod "Retention" folder with on-call friendly navigation and links to runbook.
- Alerts created in prod with correct routing (SRE primary) and documented playbooks:
  - where to look, how to confirm a real issue vs maintenance window, how to safely rerun jobs
- Post-deploy validation:
  - generate synthetic purge failures in staging and confirm alert triggers
  - validate TTL lag graphs show expected decay after backfill job runs
- Provide 2–3 customer-review friendly screenshots + explanation to GRC (Olga Petrov) for evidence package.

Notes / open questions
- Need final threshold for TTL lag paging vs ticketing by tier (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). Proposal: keep global page at p99>24h, add tier-specific tickets later.
- Determine whether request logs and audit logs have different expected lag (audit logs may have stricter expectations for evidence completeness; propose same lag threshold initially to avoid confusion).
